authors: Yunwei Ren, Yatin Dandi, Florent Krzakala, Jason D. Lee
statement: We choose Φ to be the RBF random features, because it not only is widely used, but also naturally maps far away points to near-orthogonal representations. We conjecture that any random feature mapping that has a sufficiently large high-frequency component can work here. Note that, by Assumption 9(b), if h, h′ are (pre-Φ) representations of two distinct patches, then at least one ∥hi − h′i ∥ will be at least ρ̃. Hence, ψσ (h, h′ ) ≈ 0, as long as σ ≪ ρ̃. Meanwhile, by Assumption 9(a), if h, h′ are (pre-Φ) representations of the same patch, then ψσ (h, h′ ) ≈ 1, provided that ε̃S ≪ σ. Formally, we have the following lemma, whose proof can be found in Appendix A.1.
